title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-14
content:
Summary:

Quick scratchpad capturing commands, errors, hypotheses and small repro for the KV-cache + attention-kernel selection seqlen edge-case. Seen in production (cust X) and locally when sequence length crosses certain thresholds (1024, 2048).

Symptoms:
- Intermittent crashes or device-side asserts when serving long-prefix requests (seqlen ~1025+).
- Inconsistent attention results when running warm-up vs steady-state (first tokens OK, later tokens wrong).
- Failures appear only with certain kernel selections (flash_attn_v2 / fused_attn), not with cutlass/slow reference.

Observed on:
- GPU: A100, driver: 535.xx, CUDA 12.1 (prod).
- Runtime: redwood-serving 0.9.x (branch: attention-kernel-refactor).

Repro (minimal):
1) Reproducer script (python):
   # repro_kv_seqlen.py (local)
   import torch
   from redwood_runtime import ModelServe

   model = ModelServe.load('gpt-small-test')
   prompt = 'A' * 10  # trivial prompt to build kv cache repeatedly

   # step to force long prefix
   for i in range(3):
       out = model.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=1, return_kv=True)
       prompt = prompt + 'x' * 350  # grow prefix each iter

   # final step: triggers issue when seqlen == 1025/2049
   model.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=1)

2) Run with different kernel env vars:
   # baseline (works):
   RUN_KERNEL=cutlass python repro_kv_seqlen.py

   # fails reproducibly on my machine when kernel=flash_attn_v2
   RUN_KERNEL=flash_attn_v2 python repro_kv_seqlen.py

3) Alternative: set runtime override: --attn-kernel=flash_attn_v1 vs v2

Commands I ran (local):
- python -m repro_kv_seqlen --seed 42 --batch 1 --seqlen 1025
- RUN_KERNEL=flash_attn_v2 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python -m repro_kv_seqlen
- nsys profile --output=trace -t cuda python repro_kv_seqlen.py

Example error output (cropped):
RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
  File "/opt/redwood/runtime/attention/flash_attn_v2.py", line 321, in forward
    attn = flash_attn(query, key, value, cu_seqlens, max_seqlen)
RuntimeError: cudaMemcpy HtoD failed: invalid argument

Torch printed shapes just before crash:
- query: torch.Size([1, 12, 1025, 64])
- key:   torch.Size([1, 12, 1025, 64])
- value: torch.Size([1, 12, 1025, 64])
- kv_cache.buffer_len (internal): 1024  <-- suspicious (off by one)

Additional log snippet (my instrumentation):
[2025-02-10 14:23:51,123] INFO  kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=flash_attn_v2, policy=auto, reason=seqlen>1024 && supports_flash_v2
[2025-02-10 14:23:51,124] DEBUG flash_attn_v2: using block_size=1024, num_blocks=2, pad_to=2048
[2025-02-10 14:23:51,125] ERROR flash_attn_v2: kv_index_out_of_bounds idx=1024 max_idx=1024

Initial hypothesis:
- flash_attn_v2 assumes seqlen is padded to block_size multiples (1024). When seqlen == 1025, internal indexing computed as (num_blocks * block_size) ends up referencing index == pad boundary (==1024) which is outside valid 0..seqlen-1 range. Off-by-one in block boundary calculation.
- Another possibility: KV cache ring buffer length is set to block_size (1024) in some code path, so when seqlen grows beyond that single block, writes/read indices wrap unexpectedly. The log above showing buffer_len==1024 is suspicious.

What I tried / quick experiments:
- Forced kernel to cutlass -> no crash, but 4x slower. Suggests bug is in flash implementation.
- Padding seqlen up to next multiple of 1024 (i.e., pad to 2048) before passing to flash_attn_v2 -> works (no OOB).
- Modified flash_attn_v2 to use < instead of <= in boundary check -> repro goes away locally (patched manually) but need proper upstream fix.
- Reproduced on A100 and RTX6000; not reproduced on very old kernels (pre-flash integration) where runtime uses reference attn.
- Added explicit kv_cache.grow(new_len) before final generate -> mitigates. Code path: when appending to kv cache, call ensure_capacity(seqlen) if seqlen>buffer_len. This fixed prod for one customer temporarily.

Hypotheses prioritized:
1) Kernel internal indexing bug (high confidence): flash_attn_v2 is computing block boundaries incorrectly leading to access at index==block_size when seqlen == block_size+1.
2) Kernel selection logic mismatch (medium): selector uses configured max_seqlen or previous request seqlen to decide parameters (e.g., pad_to) but then runtimes use current seqlen leading to mismatch between cu_seqlens prepared on CPU and kernel expectations.
3) KV-cache allocation bug (low-medium): ring buffer allocation uses previous max_seq or block_size but fails to reallocate for seqlen+1 due to race under concurrency.

Next-level repro & instrumentation to nail root cause:
- Add asserts in CPU prep code for cu_seqlens to ensure last cu_seqlens entry < seqlen and that total padded length == expected pad_to. Dump cu_seqlens and device-side params in debug builds.
- Rebuild flash_attn_v2 with extra bounds checks and fallback to reference when OOB detected (temp).
- Create small CUDA kernel that mimics flash block indexing and test indexing arithmetic for a range of seqlen values 1..4096 to see where off-by-one manifests.
- Run with ASAN / cuda-memcheck (slower) to get exact stack trace in kernel.

Mitigations (short-term):
- Force kernel selection to cutlass for customers hitting the bug via runtime feature flag (config: attn.kernel.force=cutlass).
- Ensure KV cache grows proactively: ensure_capacity(new_seqlen) on every new request, not lazy-only on writes.
- Add telemetry: count kernel OOB errors and tag with chosen_kernel, seqlen, model_name.

Notes / breadcrumbs from linked PRs: 
- GH PR#4521 (attention-kernel-refactor) touched block alignment code and kernel args packing. Author: @mruiz (Marco). Suspect lines: pack_cu_seqlens() changed semantics to use pad_to instead of seqlen.
- JIRA RT-987: customer incident, long prefix (up to 3000 tokens) experienced intermittent crashes; they were on flash_attn_v2.

Open TODOs:
- [ ] Add unit test in runtime that exercises seqlen crossing boundaries (1023->1024->1025) for all kernels.
- [ ] Add debug dumps for cu_seqlens and padded lengths when running in debug mode.
- [ ] Push a patch to flash_attn_v2 to guard against idx>=seqlen (fail early), then figure whether logic should pad or adjust indices.
- [ ] Coordinate with Marco (PR owner) to review pack_cu_seqlens changes.
- [ ] Roll runtime feature flag to force cutlass and monitor metrics for impact (cost and latency).

Quick logs to attach to ticket: (copy/paste)
---
INFO kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=flash_attn_v2 policy=auto seqlen=1025 model=gpt-small-test
DEBUG flash_attn_v2: block_size=1024 pad_to=2048 num_blocks=2
ERROR flash_attn_v2: kv_index_out_of_bounds idx=1024 max_idx=1024
RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
---

Personal notes: I will add an assert in pack_cu_seqlens locally and run the full test matrix (batch 1..8, seqlen 512..4096) to map failing points. If it's really just block boundary arithmetic, change should be small. If it's KV ring buffer logic, will be slightly larger.

If someone picks this up: start by reproducing locally with the provided repro script + RUN_KERNEL env override. Reach out to Marco for context on the refactor. Priya can help with nsys traces if needed.

End of scratchpad.
